And he told me that Blagoje Simic was so astonished, so embittered when I told him that, and then I took Mr. Zaric to the command --

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. How far is the command from that intersection?

utterances.speaker: TEODOR TUTNJEVIC
utterances.text: From that intersection, the command is about 1 kilometre away.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Who told you that Blagoje Simic was shocked and astonished by that event?

utterances.speaker: TEODOR TUTNJEVIC
utterances.text: That was what Mr. Zaric told me when he got into the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And you came to the command of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: TEODOR TUTNJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we came to the command of the 4th Detachment. He then called Mr. Nikolic in Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Who did you find at the command of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: TEODOR TUTNJEVIC
utterances.text: In the command of the 4th Detachment, there was Mr. Jovo Savic who was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Was Mr. Jovo Savic then the commander of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: TEODOR TUTNJEVIC
utterances.text: First he was Radovan who was the commander, and then it was Jovo. Yes. He was the commander because Radovan was not a commander for a very long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And did Simo Zaric tell Jovo Savic and other people who were at the command what had happened in Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: TEODOR TUTNJEVIC
utterances.text: Apart from Mr. Savic, there were a few other people who were there in the command, there was Mr. Mihajlo Tovirac [phoen] also known as Pile who was there. And then there was a man nicknamed Buco, I don't know his name, and there were a few other men and Simo told this, he said what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And then what did he do then?

utterances.speaker: TEODOR TUTNJEVIC
utterances.text: He called Pelagicevo, I think he spoke to Mr. Nikolic, and then I took him home, and I went home as well. And told me that the next day we would be going to Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: This conversation with the command in Pelagicevo, did Simo Zaric then talk to one person or did he talk to two people? Can you perhaps remember?

utterances.speaker: TEODOR TUTNJEVIC
utterances.text: I recall that he spoke -- I think it was Makso, it was a name called Makso that Simo spoke to him, I think. Simo called him and spoke to him. After that conversation there was Mr. Nikolic who called and I know that he was the commander because Simo called him Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Was this line interrupted or was this a different -- was it the continuous conversation and just people who were coming on to the line?

utterances.speaker: TEODOR TUTNJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You said that Makso called; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TEODOR TUTNJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did then Makso pass on to the receiver to someone else and then the conversation continued or did Simo call twice?

utterances.speaker: TEODOR TUTNJEVIC
utterances.text: No. First Simo spoke to Makso and then Makso gave either the microphone or the receiver, I don't know what, to Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So this was one conversation with two people on the other side?

utterances.speaker: TEODOR TUTNJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So you went home and what did Zaric tell you before you parted?

utterances.speaker: TEODOR TUTNJEVIC
utterances.text: He -- he said that we would be going to Pelagicevo the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And did you go and when did you go the next day?

utterances.speaker: TEODOR TUTNJEVIC
utterances.text: The next day, I think it was about 7.00 in the morning, 7 something, I took him to Pelagicevo and he went to the command, I was outside. When he left, when he went out, he said that he would have to go to Belgrade the next day. I [as interpreted] would have to go to Belgrade to somebody called Jugo Maksimovic that he would have to go see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have one correction in the transcript on page 92, line 7, the witness didn't say I would have to go to Belgrade. But Simo actually had to go to Belgrade. He.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Simo Zaric tell you that he would have to go to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: TEODOR TUTNJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He said that he would have to go to Belgrade the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You did not drive Mr. Simo Zaric to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: TEODOR TUTNJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Now we will go on to the events at the centre for reporting of the municipality of Samac. The events that took place at the end of May in 1992. What do you know and did you go and drive Mr. Simo Zaric to the centre for reporting of the municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: TEODOR TUTNJEVIC
utterances.text: I drove Mr. Zaric twice to the centre for reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: What was the first time?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, because we are talking now about one place that was already mentioned couple of times, and we used to call it communication centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Not centre for reporting, in order to avoid any confusion and misunderstanding maybe we should refer to it in the same way we usually did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The communication centre, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I think it's now time to stop for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We will adjourn and continue our proceedings tomorrow in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: 7.00 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 26th day of March, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.
